mc.q: Which of the following statements about direct access on a storage device are correct?
st: Writing the data of a file starts from the beginning of the storage device.
In general, the seek time to search for a file is faster than that of sequential access.
It is more commonly used in hard disks than sequential access.
mc.exp: Direct access jumps straight to the data, so seeking is faster, and hard disks use it. It does not need to start from the beginning.

mc.q: The following seven-segment display is widely used. Each segment is an LED light that can be turned on or off independently. Other than when all segments are turned off, how many different patterns can be generated by the display?
mc.exp: 7 segments, each on or off: 2⁷ = 128 patterns. Minus all-off: 127.

mc.q: Mary only has a computer without any network connections. Which of the following systems can she carry out?
mc.exp: Distributed processing needs a network. Real-time and batch processing can run on one computer.

mc.q: In which of the following 8-bit representations will the addition of integers 01100000 and 01100000 result in an overflow error?
mc.exp: Both are +96. 96 + 96 = 192, above the 8-bit signed maximum (127) in all three systems.

mc.q: Which of the following clauses should be used in a SELECT SQL command for displaying information where salary is greater than 5000 in ascending order of salary?
o: WHERE salary > 5000 AND ORDER BY salary
HAVING salary > 5000 OR ORDER BY salary
mc.exp: Row conditions go in WHERE (HAVING is for groups). ORDER BY is a separate clause, not joined with AND/OR; ascending is the default.

mc.q:
Consider the following pseudocode for checking a normal school exam result:
IF (MARKS >= 50) THEN
     OUTPUT 'PASS'
ELSE
     OUTPUT 'FAIL'
Which of the following sets of test values is appropriate?
mc.exp: Good test data covers both outcomes and the boundary: 99 (pass), 0 (fail) and 50 (boundary).

mc.q: Which of the following should be considered when creating a presentation for a project using presentation software?
mc.exp: Layout, colours and slide order all affect a presentation.

mc.q: When entering formulas in a spreadsheet, which of the following results is incorrect?
mc.exp: UPPER gives TECHNOLOGY, all capitals. "Technology" would be PROPER.

mc.q: Which of the following is not required for a mail merge using a word processor?
mc.exp: Mail merge needs a data source, a main document and merge fields. Field length is not needed.

mc.q: What is/are the benefit(s) of creating a report in PDF format instead of DOCX format?
st: The text format can be preserved.
mc.exp: PDF keeps the layout the same on any device. DOCX can also have hyperlinks and colour fonts.

mc.q: Which of the following image file formats support transparent background images?
mc.exp: PNG and GIF support transparency. JPG does not.

mc.q: Which of the following may involve Object Linking and Embedding (OLE)?
st: Using mail merge to create documents
Inserting images in a presentation slide
mc.exp: Mail merge links to an outside data file and inserted images can be embedded or linked. A pivot table works inside one spreadsheet.

mc.q: Which of the following regarding Unicode and Big-5 code is correct?
o: In a computer, the use of Big-5 code and Unicode depends on the operating system.
Big-5 code is used for representing characters in Chinese only.
Unicode is used for representing characters in English and other languages.
For web browsing, the use of a character set depends on the browser.
mc.exp: Unicode covers English and most other languages. Big-5 also has English letters, and the character set is set by the file, not the OS or browser.

mc.q: For a CPU with the specifications of 16 cores, 5 GHz and a 30 MB cache, which of the following are correct?
st: The clock rate of the CPU is 5 GHz.
The maximum number of programs that the CPU can handle at the same time is 16.
The CPU accesses data in the cache memory faster than that in RAM.
mc.exp: 5 GHz is the clock rate and cache is faster than RAM. Cores do not limit the number of programs; multitasking can run many more.

mc.q: Which of the following is the main function of a network interface card in a computer?
o: To connect to a wired router and project Wi-Fi signals to a designated area.
To direct data packets from one network to another network.
To filter and forward data packets from the computer to another device.
To send and receive network signals.
mc.exp: A NIC sends and receives network signals. A is an access point, B a router, C a switch/firewall.

mc.q: Which of the following are functions of an operating system?
mc.exp: The OS allocates resources and schedules jobs. Permanent storage is done by storage devices.

mc.q: Which of the following is not a specification of a projector?
mc.exp: rpm is a hard disk spindle speed, not a projector spec.

mc.q:
In a computer, the performance of each individual task is shown below:
TaskPerformance
Execution of database queriesPoor
Online meetingsSmooth
Playing of 4K videos on a hard diskFair
Which of the following components should be upgraded?
mc.exp: Online meetings are smooth, so the network is fine. Slow queries point to the CPU and weak 4K playback to the display card.

mc.q: John has just connected a new USB printer to a computer. Why is he able to use the printer immediately?
o: The RAM size of the printer is large enough to store the data for printing.
The operating system of the computer already has a driver program for the printer.
USB printers do not need driver programs.
There is a built-in CPU in the printer to manage the printing.
mc.exp: Plug and play works because the OS already has a suitable driver.

mc.q: Which of the following about the use of HTTP is correct?
o: It can convert a domain name into an IP address.
It can distinguish a wireless network from a wired network.
It can retrieve a web page from a web server.
It can encrypt and decrypt data through a secure channel.
mc.exp: HTTP transfers web pages. DNS converts names and HTTPS/SSL encrypts.

mc.q:
Peter browses a new web site and sees the following message:
[We use third-party cookies to personalize content and to analyse web traffic. Read more about cookies.  [Accept]  [Reject]]
Which of the following is/are the consequence(s) of clicking the 'Accept' button?
st: The bandwidth of the network may be decreased.
The address book of his email account may be disclosed.
mc.exp: Cookies track browsing and can collect personal information. They cannot read his email address book or cut bandwidth.

mc.q: Mary uploads a photo to her social media account through a browser. Which of the following protocols will probably be involved?
mc.exp: DNS finds the server, HTTP(S) carries the upload and IP routes the packets: all three.

mc.q:
In the following network diagram, computers can access the Internet. What are X and Y?
[Diagram: two computers — X — Y — Internet]
mc.exp: Computers connect to a switch (X), and the router (Y) links the LAN to the Internet.

mc.q: Which of the following about IP addresses is/are correct?
st: They contain location information and make network devices accessible for communication.
They are used to reassemble the data received back into the original order.
They can be used with both the Internet and Intranet.
mc.exp: IP addresses locate devices and work on both Internet and intranet. Reassembling packets is TCP's job.

mc.q: Which of the following is the common input and output of a domain name system (DNS) server?
o: Input: IP address, Output: MAC address
Input: Domain name, Output: MAC address
Input: Domain name, Output: IP address
mc.exp: DNS turns a domain name into an IP address.

mc.q: Which of following about wired networks and wireless networks is correct?
o: Wired network: A more stable connection, Wireless network: Flexible network access
Wired network: Higher network security, Wireless network: A more stable connection
Wired network: Flexible network access, Wireless network: Higher network security
Wired network: Flexible network access, Wireless network: A more stable connection
mc.exp: Wired is more stable; wireless gives flexible access.

mc.q:
Dry run the following algorithm. How many '*' are output?
N ← 2
WHILE N < 8 DO
      OUTPUT '*'
      N ← N + 3
mc.exp: N = 2 → '*', N = 5 → '*', N = 8 stops. Two stars.

mc.q:
Answer Questions 28 and 29 with reference to the following algorithms.
Algorithm 1
S ← 0
i ← 0
FOR i FROM 1 TO 5 DO
      S ← S + N[i]
OUTPUT S

Algorithm 2
S ← 0
WHILE (i <= 5) DO
      S ← S + N[i]
OUTPUT S

Suppose that all values in the array N are 2. What is the output of Algorithm 1?
mc.exp: The loop adds N[1] to N[5]: 5 × 2 = 10.

mc.q:
(Refer to the algorithms in Question 28.)
Algorithm 1
S ← 0
i ← 0
FOR i FROM 1 TO 5 DO
      S ← S + N[i]
OUTPUT S

Algorithm 2
S ← 0
WHILE (i <= 5) DO
      S ← S + N[i]
OUTPUT S

The purposes of Algorithm 1 and Algorithm 2 should be the same. What are the missing statements in Algorithm 2?
mc.exp: Algorithm 2 needs i ← 1 before the loop and i ← i + 1 inside it, like the FOR loop.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
A ← 5
B ← 11
C ← 7
FOR C FROM 2 TO 3 DO
      B ← A + B
OUTPUT (A + B)
mc.exp: The loop runs twice: B = 16, then 21. A + B = 5 + 21 = 26.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm for the input 'Y', 'N', 'Y', 'N', 'Y'?
S ← 0
FOR i FROM 1 TO 5 DO
     INPUT CH
     IF CH = 'Y' THEN
         S ← S + 1
     ELSE
         OUTPUT '#'
OUTPUT S
mc.exp: '#' is output for each N (twice) and S is only output at the end: ##3.

mc.q:
NUM is an integer array with N values. What is the purpose of the following algorithm?
i ← 1
A ← NUM[i]
WHILE i < N DO
      i ← i + 1
      IF NUM[i] > A THEN
            A ← NUM[i]
o: To count the number of values in NUM.
To calculate the sum of values in NUM.
To find the maximum value in NUM.
To find the minimum value in NUM.
mc.exp: A is replaced whenever a bigger value appears, so it ends as the maximum.

mc.q: Which of the following are advantages of using the modular approach when designing algorithms?
st: A module can be reused in other scenarios.
The execution time of an algorithm is shorter.
The modules are easier to design and test.
mc.exp: Modules are reusable and easier to design and test. They do not make the program run faster.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the advantage(s) of using open source software over freeware?
st: It is easier to set up and use.
Users can improve the source code and share it in the community.
mc.exp: Only open source lets users change and share the code. It is not always easier or cross-platform.

mc.q: Which of the following are proper measures when using social media platforms?
st: Manage the privacy settings to control who can see your posts.
Use a strong login password and change it regularly.
Be aware of what personal information you have provided.
mc.exp: All three protect your account and privacy.

mc.q: Which of the following programs can enhance the security of using a computer?
mc.exp: Firewalls and encryption protect the computer. Adware shows ads and can be a risk.

mc.q: Which of the following can help bridge the digital divide?
st: Providing free access to computers in public libraries.
Providing Internet access for students in need.
Providing online English lessons for students in need.
mc.exp: Free computers and Internet access close the gap in IT access. Online English lessons need access already and teach English, not IT.

mc.q: What is/are the advantage(s) of using Secure Socket Layer (SSL) on web sites?
st: The data transfer rate is higher.
The IP addresses of the web sites can be hidden.
mc.exp: SSL encrypts data. It does not speed things up or hide IP addresses.

mc.q: Why do many companies prefer commercial software to open source software?
st: Open source software contains more software bugs.
Commercial software developers can provide better support.
Open source software cannot be modified by companies.
mc.exp: Companies value vendor support. Open source is not necessarily buggier, and it can be modified.

mc.q: How can updating an operating system frequently protect computers from virus attacks?
o: More support from the developer of the operating system can be provided.
The computer performance can be enhanced.
A virus check can be conducted.
mc.exp: Updates patch security holes that viruses use.

lq.stem: Mary plans to upgrade her laptop computer.

parts.q: Give two benefits of replacing the hard disk with an SSD as the secondary storage of the computer.
parts.ms:
Faster seek time / shock resistance / lighter in weight / less heat produced during operation / less power consumption / smaller in size (1×2)
✗ more silence in operation (not related to the scenario)

parts.q: Mary plans to increase the size of RAM to enhance the computational power of the computer. What is the main function of RAM? How can it enhance the computational power of the computer?
parts.ms:
RAM temporarily stores user programs / data (1)
Increasing the size of RAM can decrease time needed to access the secondary storage devices. (1)

parts.q:
Mary chooses one of the following methods for using a word processor:
Method 1: She uses a word processor that runs on a browser.
Method 2: She installs a word processor on her laptop computer.
Other than cost, give a benefit of each method.
Method 1: ______
Method 2: ______
parts.ms:
Method 1: Updated functions are provided. / No installation is required. / The word processor can be used on any other computer. (1)
Method 2: No Internet connection is required. / More functions can be provided. (1)

parts.q: She finally chooses Method 2. However, she finds that she cannot install the software successfully. Give two possible reasons for this.
parts.ms:
Not compatible with the operating system
Not enough storage space (1×2)

parts.q:
Mary and her classmate Peter are working on a project for a competition and have the following conversation.
Peter: I've found some useful information and images on the Internet for our project.
Mary: I'm not sure that the information you've found is reliable.
Suggest two ways of validating the information found by Peter.
parts.ms:
Cross check with different sources
Check from authoritative sources.
Check the date/time of the publication. (1×2)

parts.q: In terms of copyright, what should they do before using the images in their project? Give two suggestions for them.
parts.ms:
Acknowledge/identify/label the source.
Get consent from provenance.
Pay for the usage.
Use Open Source/copyleft/Creative Commons (CC) information and images. (1×2)

lq.stem:
Ms Ng uses the following spreadsheet to record the progress of her students in a reading scheme. The cut-off date and basic score are stored in C102 and E102 respectively.
ABCDEF
1StudIDBook codeCompletion dateLevelValidScore
2S01C00131/12/2021214
3S29C2344/3/2022302
4S29E4561/1/2022402
5S03C90030/4/2021517
6S01E2331/12/2021416
⋮⋮⋮⋮⋮⋮⋮
101
102Cut-off date31/12/2021Basic score2

parts.q: If a student can complete the reading on or before the cut-off date in C102, the value 1 will be shown in Column E, and 0 if otherwise. A formula is entered into E2 and then copied to E3:E100. Write down the formula in E2.

The values in Column F are students' scores. They are calculated based on E102, Column D and Column E, as shown below:
Score = Level × Valid + Basic score
A formula is entered into F2 and then copied to F3:F100. Write down the formula in F2.

Ms Ng uses a pivot table to find the sum of the scores for each student. Complete the following part for creating the pivot table.
COLUMNS: ______ VALUES: ______
parts.ms:
COLUMNS: StudID (1)
VALUES: sum of Score / sum(Score) (1, 1)
① use of sum
① Score/score

parts.q: Ms Ng converts A1:F100 in the spreadsheet to a database table REC. Suggest a primary key for REC.
parts.ms: StudID + Book code (1)

parts.q:
Based on the given 5 records on the spreadsheet, what is the output after executing the following SQL statement? 
SELECT StudID, SUM(Score) FROM REC
WHERE Valid = 1
GROUP BY StudID
parts.ms:
S01 10
S03 7 (2)
① group by + where
① sum + select + other fields

parts.q: Ms Ng plans to display the top 5 students who have the highest scores using a chart in presentation software. Draft a chart to illustrate the presentation clearly and concisely.
parts.ms:
chart type (1)
title, legend, axis title, axis label, data label (any 2) (1×2)

lq.stem:
Eva writes a subprogram with the following pseudocode to sort an array A. 
Line  Content
1     i ← 1
2     j ← 2
3     while i < 5 do
4         if A[i] >= A[i-1] then
5             i ← j
6             j ← j + 1
7         else
8             swap the contents of A[i] and A[i-1]
9             i ← i - 1
10            if i = 0 then
11                i ← 1

parts.q:
Suppose that the initial content of A is:
A[0]A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]
43186
TEMP is a variable. Complete the following pseudocode to represent Line 8. 
TEMP ← A[i]
______
______
parts.ms:
A[i] ← A[i-1]
A[i-1] ← TEMP (1)

parts.q:
What are the contents of A, i and j after completing the first, second and third iterations of the loop (Lines 3 to 11)?
First iteration: A[0]–A[4] ______ i: ____ j: ____
Second iteration: A[0]–A[4] ______ i: ____ j: ____
Third iteration: A[0]–A[4] ______ i: ____ j: ____
parts.ms:
First iteration: A = 3, 4, 1, 8, 6 (1); i:1 j:2 (1)
Second iteration: A = 3, 4, 1, 8, 6 (1); i:2 j:3 (1)
Third iteration: A = 3, 1, 4, 8, 6 (1); i:1 j:3

parts.q:
Set 1 and Set 2 below are two sets of values as the initial content of A. How many times will Line 8 be executed for each set?
Set 1
A[0]A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]
23579
Set 2
A[0]A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]
97532
Set 1: ______ Set 2: ______
On Line 10, there will be no changes in the result of the subprogram if 'i = 0' is changed to 'i <= 0'. Why?
parts.ms: i will never be smaller than 0. (1)

parts.q:
Below are three sets of test data as the initial content of A. Choose two sets for testing the subprogram and explain briefly. 
Test 1: -3, -1, 4, 0, 7
Test 2: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Test 3: 1, 1, 3, 3, 5
parts.ms:
Test 1: It contains negative values / zero.
Test 2: It is sorted / unsorted / normal / standard data.
Test 3: It contains duplicate values. (1×2)

lq.stem: David operates a toy shop in a shopping centre.

parts.q: David sets up a computer network in the toy shop. Name two transmission media for a wired network.
parts.ms:
Twisted pair cable
Unshielded Twisted Pair cable / UTP
Shielded Twisted Pair cable / STP
fibre optics / fiber optics / optical fiber
Coaxial cable (1×2)
✗ Network cable / TP

parts.q: In the network, David uses a switch instead of a router. Give a reason for this.
parts.ms:
He would like to form one single network. / Connect all the devices used in his toy shop that a switch is used to connect devices and help one device communicate with another devices. (1)
✗ port

parts.q: David considers changing the toy shop from a physical shop to an online shop. State a benefit and a drawback of this change and explain briefly.
parts.ms:
Benefit: Access to worldwide markets / anytime (1)
✗ Improve competitiveness / minimal sales cost (with explanation)
Drawback: No face-to-face interaction / Additional cost on building web servers (1)

parts.q: David has set up mytoyshop.com for customers to order toys. He considers providing an HTTPS connection with the URL https://mytoyshop.com . What should David apply for and obtain before he can implement an HTTPS connection?
parts.ms:
Digital Cert / SSL / TLS / e-cert (1)
✗ domain name

parts.q:
A public and private key encryption system is used in the web site. Who should use the public key and private key respectively?
Public key: ______
Private key: ______
parts.ms:
Public key: customers / users (1)
Private key: David (1)

parts.q:
David uses robots to retrieve toys from a warehouse. The robots are controlled by 5-bit commands, where part of the commands are shown below:
CommandDescription
00000Stop
01111Start
01001Turn 90° clockwise
10000Turn 90° anti-clockwise
11001Move 1 step forward
10111Move 1 step backward
During data transmission, an error bit may occur. Briefly describe how this error can be checked.
parts.ms:
Add a parity bit for checking / use checksum / Transmit two times to check the consistency of data. (1)
✗ validation check

parts.q:
David considers using 2-bit commands to control the robots, as shown below:
CommandDescription
00Stop
11Start
10Turn 90° clockwise
01Move 1 step forward
Write the five 2-bit commands below to take the action 'Move 1 step backward'.
11 ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ 00
parts.ms:
10 10 01 10 10 (2)
① for the underlined part 10 10 01

parts.q: What is the benefit of using 2-bit commands instead of 5-bit commands to control the robots?
parts.ms:
The design of the machine can be simplified / Fewer commands are implemented / The performance is better due to the simple and limited number of commands / The response will be faster as the CPU on the robot does not have to decode too many bits at a time / The instructions will be transferred and processed faster when controlling the robot (1)
✗ smaller storage space is needed

lq.stem:
John sets up a fitness centre and considers the following three methods of identifying members:
(1) A smart card
(2) A plastic card with a printed QR code
(3) A mobile application installed in members' mobile phones

parts.q: Give an advantage of (1) over (2).
parts.ms: Smart card is more secure than QR code. / Smart card is harder to replicate while QR code can be replicated more easily. (1)

parts.q: Give an advantage of (2) over (1).
parts.ms: Using QR code is cheaper (lower cost) / It is easier to implement (manufacture) QR code (1)

parts.q: Give an advantage of (3) over (1) and (2).
parts.ms: More / additional functions can be provided in the mobile application. (e.g. View profile, records of the use of fitness centres, check the validity of membership, amend Personal Data.) / No need to carry the card. (1)

parts.q:
John plans to provide a device for each member to monitor their heartbeat rates. The device is connected to a server so that his staff can remotely collect members' heartbeat rates. Each device continuously records and stores the heartbeat rates in a data file. Every 5 minutes the data file will be uploaded to the server.
Is this arrangement a batch processing system or a real time system? Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
It is a batch processing system as (1)
- data is recorded and collected over a period of time and uploaded to the server.
- it contains continuously gaining a total amount of data and upload the date file at a single log.
- it does not process up-to-date data but process data once every 5 minutes
- data is transferred periodically but not immediately.
✗ it is scheduled to upload data every 5 minutes.

parts.q: The data files are 2KB each. The network bandwidth acquired by the fitness centre is 10 Mbps. When 200 members upload their data files at the same time, how long will it take in total? Show your calculation.
Give two potential problems of using WiFi to upload the data files to the server.
parts.ms:
- Security problem e.g. eavesdropping
- Unstable connection (1×2)

parts.q:
The fitness centre provides livestreamed fitness lessons for members to join at home.
A member complains that the streaming of videos is sometimes not smooth, though the bandwidth of his broadband connection is sufficiently large for streaming. Why?
parts.ms: There is interference from the environment. / Too many members view the lessons at the same time, and the network traffic becomes very heavy. (1)

parts.q: John decides to record videos of the lessons for members to download. Other than solving the problem in (c)(i), give a benefit of his decision.
parts.ms:
The delivered message can be edited before broadcasting. / Subtitles can be inserted. / It can be viewed at any time or multiple times. / It can be viewed in offline mode or without an Internet connection. (1)
✗ Members can choose lessons they want to attend.
✗ Watch the video with friends later.

parts.q:
John receives the email below:
To:
From: survey@HKSAR.com.hk
Subject: From HKSAR Government
Please complete the following survey:
Link to survey
Explain briefly why it is probably a scam email. Describe what harmful consequence might happen after clicking the link.
parts.ms:
The email comes from a .com domain which is commercial / The email does not come from a .gov domain (1)
Users will be directed to phishing web site after clicking the link. (1)
Other reasonable answers:
Triggering the download of malware to the device
Downloading and installing malware, resulting in the leakage of personal information
Getting infected with ransomware
Triggering the download of a virus into his computer or network
